title: Agent cluster and crash recovery: specifications?

labels.name: topic: agent
labels.description: The interaction with JavaScript's agent and agent cluster concepts

body:
Are there existing efforts, and if not, should there be, to standardize the "recover from a crashed tab" workflow? Also, this could be broadened to "how to recover from a crashed agent-cluster?". 

For example, if the agent cluster that crashes belong to an auxiliary top-level BC, if the UA shows some sort of "would you like to reload the crashed page" dialog, should it be reloaded as the original auxiliary, or as a brand new top-level that has been loaded in response to user interaction?

What if the crash occurs in a different agent-cluster from that of the top-level BC, for example if it contains a cross-site iframe running in another agent-cluster.

If a shared-worker agent-cluster crashes, should the UA try to recover from it? If so, how would that be noticeable to users of the worker in other agent-clusters? I can imagine some sort of `onfailure` event that would fire on the `SharedWorker` to alert any users of the failure, and give them an opportunity to restart a new one, or the "restart" could be transparent to the user, at the risk of some inconsistency in state. 

With service-worker, crashes could even occur while there are no documents shown to the user, and such a crash could affect the ability of a document for that origin to do what it wants to do when it is loaded in a tab later(this is probably something best discussed in the context of the SW spec).  

The general idea is that since the spec is moving towards formalizing the use of agent-clusters, and those imply processes, which implies "the UA can recover from a crash of such process", which means that it might make sense to start speccing what such recovery exactly entails, since the effects of the recovery, or lack thereof, are also potentially noticeable from script.
